videos.title: The Minecraft Glitch That Broke the Entire Internet #minecraft #log4shell #log4j #cybersecurity
videos.description:
In December 2021, one of the most severe security flaws in internet history was discovered — through Minecraft. Players noticed that typing a specific string of text into Minecraft's chat could crash servers or even let attackers run their own code on them. The cause was a critical flaw in Log4j, a Java logging library used almost everywhere — from Minecraft to Amazon, Apple iCloud, Twitter, and countless enterprise systems worldwide. Because Log4j quietly logs almost everything, including user input, attackers could plant malicious code inside a simple chat message, username, or web request, and the server would execute it automatically just by logging it. Within days, hackers were scanning the entire internet for vulnerable systems. Security teams worldwide worked around the clock patching servers before attackers could exploit them at scale. It became known as Log4Shell — one bug, buried in a tool nobody thought twice about, that put a huge share of the internet at risk.
